real_messages.fact: US Airways 1549 (Airbus A320-214): "The airplane was equipped with a GPWS, which contained both GPWS and enhanced GPWS functions. From 1529:14.9 to 1530:40.1, the two systems transmitted a total of 15 alerts, including altitude alerts and the following: “too low, terrain;” “too low, gear;” “terrain, terrain, pull up;” and “caution terrain.”"

A320 FCOM quoted by NTSB: "An aural low-energy “SPEED SPEED SPEED” warning, repeated every 5 seconds, warns the pilot that the aircraft’s energy level is going below a threshold ..." — available in normal law in CONF 2, CONF 3 or full flaps; in US1549 it was inhibited by GPWS warnings (alert prioritisation).

A320 CVR transcript (US1549) labels: "FWC [sound of single chime]", "FWC [sound of continuous repetitive chime for 9.6 seconds ...]", "EGPWS terrain terrain. pull up. pull up.", "GPWS too low. gear.", "GPWS (fifty or thirty)", "FWC retard." — i.e. the RETARD callout is generated by the FWC, altitude numbers attributed to GPWS by NTSB.

Boeing 737-7H4 (Southwest 1248) CVR transcript labels: "CAM [sound similar to altitude warning horn]" (several times during descent), "[sound similar to ACARS chime]", "[sound similar to single chime]", "[sound similar to double chime]", and after the overrun "CAM [sound similar to stick shaker]".

Turkish Airlines TK1951 (Boeing 737-800): the faulty left radio altimeter "causes a total of five audible warnings to be heard in the cockpit"; autothrottle went to "retard flare" mode; "Once the speed reduced to 109 knots, the stick shaker was activated, a warning that the aircraft is travelling too slowly" (narration of the Dutch Safety Board animation, ASR transcript).

observations: Measured (not sourced): A319 F-GRXM manual landing — callouts 500/400/300/200/100 then 50,40,30,20 at ~1.0-1.3 s spacing, then RETARD repeated 4x at ~1.2-1.3 s intervals (86.07, 87.04, 88.36, 89.52 s).
Measured (not sourced): P-8A intermittent horn after touchdown — ~0.21 s on, 0.52 s period, harmonic partials every ~200 Hz from ~600 Hz to >4 kHz.

Template matching showed the A319 CDG and Adria A319 FWC voices match each other (r 0.2-0.33 in noise); the P-8A and Transaero 737NG EGPWS callouts match each other (r 0.31-0.46) → same voice set on P-8A and 737NG.
